Lightning risk map (tap to open / close) Conditional on detected lightning. This is not overall wildfire risk.
Each square = a 0.1° cell (about 11 km) with lightning in the last 24 h. Colour = chance that a reported lightning-caused fire follows in the 3x3 cells around it within the next 3 days. The % is conditional on lightning in that cell: a reported lightning-caused fire anywhere in the 3x3 cells (about 33 km) within 3 days counts. It is not the chance that one strike starts a fire, not the chance of any wildfire, and not human-caused fires. About 1 in 4 lightning fires (more in the far north) have no ground lightning nearby beforehand, so this map cannot show them. Hover a square for its inputs.

Covers Canadian land up to 66°N. Lightning north of 66°N and outside Canada is not scored. Dashed outline = Yukon/NT/Nunavut (less certain; the model was tested there with fewer fires). Tested 2023-24: in the North, Saskatchewan and Yukon the shown % runs about 1.4-1.9x too high; in October it runs too low. Treat those as rough.
